**Deferred one round by the `domain:metadata` seat — hot-file serialization, not priority.** Recording it so a later sweep does not read this card as simply unpicked. It is a strong card: symptom, three composing root-cause sites, a control that isolates the seam, and a stale-premise re-check already done.

**Why deferred:** the repair lands in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` — the runtime write door has to reach `expandViewContainer`, and that door is in `protocol.ts`, which is held right now by #7774 (dispatched 04:03Z, `metaItemKey` discriminator). That file took **6 merges in a single day** recently; two agents in it at once produce conflicts that cost more than the wait.

**Serial queue on `protocol.ts` as of 04:0xZ:** #7774 (in flight) → #7491 → **#7736** → #6504 → #4716.

**What is already established, so the next dispatch does not re-derive it:**

- ⚠️ **Anchor on function names, never line numbers.** This card's own body already flags that its line anchors moved between the QA run and re-verification. `protocol.ts` drifts within hours. The named symbols are `isAggregatedViewContainer`, `expandViewContainer`, `normalizeViewMetadata`, `MetadataManager.getViewsByObject`.
- **The shared question is worth answering once.** #7163 (closed) was the same missing-expansion class at the nested-plugin loader seam and was fixed *at that seam*. This is the third time the question "where does container expansion belong so every producer gets it" comes up. ⇒ Whoever dispatches this should decide deliberately between **fixing this seam** (cheap, consistent with #7163's precedent) and **moving expansion to a single choke point every producer passes** (fixes the class) — and if the second, that is a shape decision that should be ruled or escalated, ⛔ not left to the dev.
- `getViewsByObject`'s filter is **by design** — its docblock says it returns only expanded ViewItems and never the aggregated container. So the repair is to make expansion happen, ⛔ **not** to loosen that filter. A fix that makes the container itself pass the by-object filter would be treating the symptom.

**Dev report relayed by the PM** (its container is 403 on the whole GitHub API — the second attempt returned the sharper *"org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App"*). It read this card in the web UI via `WebFetch`, so its verdict is against the full body.

## ⚠️ Disclosure: I merged PR #8257 against the dev's stated instruction

Its report ends *"Open the PR as draft; I did not enable auto-merge and did not flip ready."* **I never saw that** — the dev could not open a PR, so I created #8257 myself from its pushed branch with a body I wrote, reviewed the diff, and merged it as **`0e1f6679b4`**.

This is now the **second** time in one shift (the same happened on #8258/#8037), which makes it a process gap rather than an accident: **a 403-blocked dev puts its merge conditions in the PR body, and reconstructing that body from the branch loses them.** ⇒ Recorded on the seat post: **when opening a PR on a blocked dev's behalf, ask for its intended PR body first, and treat "draft" as the default until the dev says otherwise.**

On the merits the merge stands — the diff was reviewed, CI was fully green, and the report below confirms the change is what I judged it to be. But the instruction existed and I overrode it unknowingly, so it goes on the record.

## The verdict: wrong-source bug — ⛔ not an unbuilt capability

`premise_still_valid: true`, and **every claim reproduced independently before the dev read the card.**

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Write a `defineView` container via `saveMetaItem` | accepted |
| Stored body | verbatim — `list`, `listViews`, `name`; no `object`, no `viewKind` |
| `getMetaItem` by name | present, badged `_diagnostics: {valid: true}` |
| `getMetaItems({type:'view'})` | **0** |
| Switcher predicate (`viewKind && object===`) | **0** |
| **Control** — flat `ViewItem` written the same way | **1 served, 1 switcher match** ✅ |
| **Well-formedness** — expand the stored body | **2 items, both would match the switcher** |

⭐ That last row is what decides the triage. The stored container **is well-formed** — it expands cleanly into exactly the items the switcher wants. So this is neither a malformed write nor #7893's "read path never built": **the read path exists and demonstrably works** (the control proves it), and the expansion capability exists too, applied at **two of three** entry points (`objectql/engine.ts` boot loop, `metadata/plugin.ts` artifact/HMR loader — both green). **The runtime door is the third seam and skipped it.** That is the #7163 shape this card itself named.

⭐ It also reports correcting itself: it initially leaned toward a **design exit**, on the grounds that `expandViewContainer` hard-codes `scope:'package'` while `sys_view_definition` forbids that value at runtime. Reading the card corrected it — the repro is a **writable runtime package**, where package scope is right and `sys_view_definition` is the wrong store to reason about. Stating the abandoned hypothesis is worth as much as the conclusion.

## ⭐ The trap it avoided — and this is the valuable part

Two tempting wrong fixes, both rejected with reasons:

1. **Loosen the `getMetaItems` container filter.** That filter drops containers from enumeration on a stated invariant — *"the registrar expands it into independent ViewItems"* — **true for source-registered rows, false for runtime-written ones.** Loosening it would surface the legacy wrapper to every list consumer **while still showing the switcher nothing.** Filter left untouched.
2. **Fix at a read exit.** There are **two independent object-bound readers**: REST `/meta/view?object=` goes through `getMetaItems`, but `getViewsByObject()` reads `MetadataManager.list`. Fixing either one fixes the literal repro **and leaves its sibling empty — exactly #7556's shape.**

So the fix went to `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`, documented in-repo as *"the ONE choke point all three hydration callers (boot, read-side, write-through) already share."* One expansion there serves every reader, **survives restart** (the card noted restart didn't help), and preserves read-your-writes. ⛔ Nothing extra is persisted — one byte-identical row, expansion derived on hydration, so an edited container leaves no stale rows.

## Reverse-verification (fix disabled at the call site)

| Case | Fix on | Fix off | Attribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serves expanded ViewItems | ✓ | 🔴 | headline |
| Serves the stored container, not a default | ✓ | 🔴 | anti-substitution |
| No-container object stays empty | ✓ | 🔴¹ | anti-vacuity |
| Container never enumerated (ADR-0017) | ✓ | ✓ | filter untouched |
| Independent `ViewItem` unchanged | ✓ | ✓ | not "serve whatever exists" |
| Container stored byte-identical | ✓ | ✓ | nothing extra persisted |

¹ red on its **positive** half (`crm_lead` → 2); its anti-vacuity half (`crm_account` → empty) holds under **both** arms — which is what proves the fixtures distinguish *authored-container* from *no-container*.

Gates, all post-merge and after a completed build (⛔ never concurrent with dogfood): metadata-protocol 76/1102 · metadata 31/603 · objectql 192/3400 · rest 103/1731 · runtime 145/2195 · dogfood 99 files/673 · `check:type-check-debt` exit 0 on a built closure, **no ledger entry raised, nothing `--lower`ed** · `check:nul-bytes` OK · `check:empty-changeset` OK · eslint clean.

## Out-of-scope finding, now filed

**#8285** — ADR-0017 §3.4 cites `packages/platform-objects/src/metadata/sys-view-definition.object.ts`, **which does not exist**; the object is at `packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-view-definition.object.ts`. Out of the dev's region, so reported not fixed; it cited no number in the commit rather than invent one.

⭐ **This card is the sixth instance of "a 200 that means nothing happened"** — publish succeeded at every step and produced nothing a user could see. That family (#7893, #8018, `reassignOrphanedMetadata`, #7823, #7736, #8284) is carried on the seat post as an open convention question for the maintainer.
